To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the mean score of social supports for women was moderate.
the social support for women of childbearing age in Iran is high.

the mean score of social perceived support among women of reproductive ages in Isfahan, Iran was 134.2 ± 17 and the highest and lowest mean scores of the social support dimensions were “worth” and “social integration” respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the social support for women of childbearing age, which has been neglected in the literature, especially in the Middle East.
the relationship between the social support and sociodemographic characteristics among Iranian women of reproductive age.
the relationship between social support and its predictors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
social support for Iranian reproductive-aged women was affected by sociodemographic factors, especially education level and spouse’s occupation.

sociodemographic factors affect perceived social support and could, therefore, be considered in planning and implementation of interventions to improve social supports for Iranian women of reproductive age.
education, spouse’s occupational status, sufficiency of income for household expenses and the primary support source were significant predictors of social support in Iranian women.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the women who are educated, have sufficient income for their expenses and whose spouse is employed have higher social support.
the social support for Iranian married women is moderate and the social support is affected by the women’s education, husband’s occupation, and the sufficiency of income for their expenses.
women of reproductive age who are married and with higher education, and have a sufficient income and spouse with higher occupation, have higher social support.
The main takeaway from our work is that
social support is an important factor for women's health and well-being.
social support is not a static construct.
social support is an essential component in improving women's health, and it can be improved by addressing the sociodemographic factors that are associated with social support.
